title: Vanishing Point (CBC)
paragraphs: CBC's imaginative anthology moves between science fiction, horror, psychological drama, mystery, and fantasy, using both original plays and literary adaptations to explore the border between reality and the strange.

CBC speculative-drama anthology created and produced by Bill Lane and hosted by David Calderisi. The regular first two seasons mixed original Canadian radio plays with adaptations across science fiction, horror, thriller, psychological drama and other speculative forms.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: First regular anthology season (October 5, 1984 to May 24, 1985) on [[org|org.vp.4ad028d3bc03e0f3|CBC Radio]] and Second regular anthology season (September 30, 1985 to June 30, 1986) on [[org|org.vp.4ad028d3bc03e0f3|CBC Radio]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Steve Petch (writer and radio adaptor), Tim Wynne-Jones (radio adaptor and writer), Alberto Manguel (radio adaptor), Alfred Silver (writer), Arthur Samuels (radio adaptor), Carol Bolt (writer), and Christina Meeker (writer).

The stories often return to speculative fiction and altered reality, psychological disturbance and perception, original Canadian radio drama, literary adaptation for radio, science fiction and future technology, and horror, uncanny and supernatural experience.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Open Wide binaural experiment, CBC launches Vanishing Point as Nightfall follow-up, First regular anthology season, and Second regular anthology season.
